newsitem.title: INDIA: Investors cool toward India divestment list.
newsitem.headline: Investors cool toward India divestment list.

text.p: Investment and securities firms gave a cool reception to the list of six state-run companies that the government announced on Thursday it will sell shares in.
"We would rather wait for bluer chip firms," V. Sivakumar, head of research at Peregrine Capital India Ltd said.
"Portfolio investors are unlikely to buy these firms," said a strategist in a European brokerage in Bombay.

The government named Bharat Aluminium Company Ltd, telecommunicaitons firm ITI Ltd, teleprinter maker HTL Ltd, Bongaingaon Refinery and Petrochemicals Ltd and Madras Fertilisers Ltd and Manganese Ore India Ltd, the Press Trust of India (PTI) reported from Delhi.

PTI said the divestment commission had recommended sale of 100 percent equity in HTL, upto 74 percent in Bharat Aluminium, ITI and Bongaigaon Refineries and 50 percent in Madras Fertilisers and Manganese Ore India Ltd.
"Most of them are second or third-rung PSUs (public sector units) who are not leaders in their industries or are in product lines that are not exciting," said an equities analyst.
"As far as the domestic market is concerned, the divestment programme unlikely to make much headway," said Chetan Ahya, economist at Caspian Securities.
"International investors will look only for quality issues and the issue likely to be regarded most favourably will be the IOC issue," Ahya said.
A keenly-awaited $350 million issue of international equity from largest refiner Indian Oil Corporation (IOC) is due to be launched around September, investment bankers said.

India plans to raise $1.3 billion in 1997/98 (April/March) by selling shares in state-run firms including IOC, Gas Authority of India, Modern Food Industries and India Tourism Development Corporation.
"Quality companies will be able to go ahead. The divestment will be a selective success -- so, all in all, targets for the year are likely to be missed," Ahya said.
